paper.title: MobileSteward: Integrating Multiple App-Oriented Agents with Self-Evolution to Automate Cross-App Instructions
paper.central_claim: App-oriented multi-agent scheduling, evaluation and persistent expertise/task-guideline memories improve cross-app automation and continuously optimize MobileSteward.

gap.author_gap: Procedure-oriented mobile agents struggle with cross-app dependencies, diverse app interfaces and error propagation.
gap.checked_gap: App-specific roles and separate scheduling/execution memories address a concrete coordination and specialization bottleneck; memory as a generic idea predates this work.

lineage.relation: StaffAgent is built from this GUI executor.
Prior app exploration and hierarchical/transition memory.

gap.closest_adjacent: MobileAgent-v2 plus app-memory methods, checked only through authors’ descriptions and reported baseline results.
gap.residue: Cross-app DAG scheduling plus specialized, evolving memories rather than one procedural executor.
gap.stakes: Long GUI chains fail through wrong app choice and upstream information loss.
gap.method_response: App-specialized staff, explicit flow graph, success-derived expertise and guideline stores.
gap.remaining_gap: No frozen-store isolated holdout, matched search/maintenance budget, robust admission or scaling/forgetting evaluation.
unresolved: Request shared fixed originals of MobileGPT, AutoDroid, AppAgent and MobileAgent-v2 to verify fine-grained gap/novelty; no web lookup performed.

claims.text: MobileSteward improves mobile task automation versus baseline frameworks.
claims.setting: CAPBench 14 apps; SAPBench 50 tasks; GPT-4v/4o; Pixel simulator
claims.selection_vs_test: Prior evolution on remaining CAPBench; sampled test also updates memory.
claims.result/denominator: CAPBench GPT-4o SR .59 versus MobileAgent-v2 .21; 50 per 2/3/4-app complexity (150 test); SAPBench SR .78 versus .64.
counterevidence: Unmatched budget and online state make causal attribution narrower than end-to-end comparison.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported higher observed success in these environments, not isolated proof all gain comes from retained memory.

claims.text: Self-evolution of memories improves subsequent performance.
claims.setting: CAPBench ablation and staff expertise analysis
claims.selection_vs_test: Construction initially separate, test memories continue updating.
claims.result/denominator: Table 3 SR .55 versus .50; per-condition count not separately stated; no repeated stream variance.
counterevidence: Combined memory/loop ablation, no frozen/offline-only store test or gate/curator comparison.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Memory evolution is associated with a five-point SR improvement under the reported adaptive protocol; independent retained transfer not cleanly established.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported system success improves on mobile benchmarks and combined evolution ablation favors memory, but adaptive test updates and unmatched budget do not cleanly certify retained gains on an independent frozen evaluation.
unresolved: Judge reliability, online/frozen separation, stream variance, full evolution cost; figure-only expertise values not available.
